## TL;DR

I walked the Agents page QA surface at 375, 768 and 1280px with the existing headless WebKit fixture harness. The existing harness (from the earlier #1223 pass) already covered the agent list, Model providers, Model routing, Scheduled Tasks, Reminders and Build Your Team, and all 30 of those cases passed. The gap was the paused state: the budget allowlist's paused agent and paused model rows were not rendered in any browser case. I added a case for that state at all three widths. It failed at 375px and 768px, so I fixed the layout in `BudgetControlsPanel.vue`. The new case passes at all three widths, and the existing suites still pass.

## Work and rationale

The task asks for a sweep of layout, wording and state bugs with the key-missing and paused states in scope. I started from the existing QA test rather than writing a second harness, because it already mounts the real components in jsdom and renders their markup in headless WebKit against the built global stylesheet. Keeping one harness means the new case gets the same overflow audit and the same fixed 375/768/1280 viewports.

The key-missing states were already covered by the earlier pass, and their copy reads correctly: "Not set", "Saved", "Couldn't check" and the masked password field all match the code. So I focused the new work on the paused state.

The new case builds a budget allowlist with two pauses. One is a whole-agent pause (`claude code`) with a long reason and a resume date. The other is a per-model pause (`opencode` / `deepseek v4`) with its own reason and date. It then expands the `opencode` row and checks three things at each width: nothing runs off the viewport, the paused chip stays inside its row card, and no chip overlaps a button in its row.

At 375px and 768px the case failed on two separate layout problems:

1. The header button reserved a fixed 188px on the right, to make room for the Pause/Resume and Remove buttons pinned in the row's top-right corner. The paused chip used `white-space: nowrap` and the reason used `text-overflow: ellipsis`. At 375px the reason ran past the card edge, so I let the chip wrap within the header's content box and dropped the ellipsis. The resume date sits after the reason, so it must stay readable.
2. At 768px the chip overlapped the pinned "Resume agent" button. Its left edge sits at 96px from the right with a width of about 100px, so it needs about 200px of clearance. I raised the reserve to 212px.

The reserve is the real root cause, and it cannot work on a phone. At 375px the row is about 299px wide, so 212px of reserve left a 63px text column. The chip shrank to 39px and wrapped one letter per line. Below the app's existing 720px breakpoint I now let the row actions drop under the header in normal flow, and the header keeps its full width. I checked for the same fixed-reserve pattern in the sibling Agents-page components, and no other component had it.

I also looked at the native `title` attributes on this surface. The provider "As of" span carries one, and AGENTS.md forbids native tooltips in new UI. A unit test (`model-providers-panel.test.ts`, #0625) asserts that title on purpose, so I did not remove it in this pass. Removing it would change tested behaviour, and the right replacement is a styled popover, which is a small design choice of its own. I left it in place and am flagging it below. I also confirmed that the other `title` hits on this surface are dialog props or sit inside an HTML comment, so they do not render as tooltips.

## Approaches tried

My first attempt kept the fixed corner reserve and only made the chip wrap. The overflow failure at 375px went away, but the chip still overlapped the button. Its rectangle showed the chip was 39px wide and 1326px tall, because the header content box was only 63px wide at that width. Wrapping cannot fix a column that narrow, so I changed the layout at phone widths rather than adjusting the number again.

My second attempt raised the reserve from 188px to 212px. That fixed the 768px overlap but not 375px, for the reason above. The mobile breakpoint change is what made 375px pass.

## Challenges and blockers

The first run of the QA file failed to load. Vitest used the root config, which has no Vue plugin, so every `.vue` import failed. The UI tests need `--config src/ui-app/vite.config.ts`. This is not a regression, and the repo's own `bun run test` already uses that config.

The file on disk changed twice while I was editing. Once was my own import addition. The other was the provider-panel revert, which I did on purpose.

I did not declare a `## Shots` entry. The preview board's `state` fixtures do not include a budget allowlist with paused rows, so a declared shot would show the unpaused board and would not show the change. The reviewer should check this through the new fixture case, or a human can ask for a preview of the Budget Controls tab with a paused agent.

Real-key handling was not involved. The test fixtures use fake reasons and a synthetic future date, and no key values appear anywhere.

## Key learnings

A fixed padding reserve for absolutely pinned buttons looks fine at one width and breaks at every other. The wide-screen fix was right, but the phone case needed a different layout, not a bigger number.

Table-driven WebKit cases catch what jsdom cannot. The jsdom budget tests passed throughout, because they do not measure geometry. The overlap and card-edge checks only fail in a real layout engine.

The fixture harness needed one small extension: `snapshotPanel` now accepts extra stubs, so a component whose child fetches data can be rendered without a network call.

Open items for a human decision: the provider "As of" native tooltip (a styled popover would replace the removed-title test assertion), and the focus ring on shared buttons, which uses a border-colour ring and may be low-contrast. I did not change either in this pass.
